intro: Looking for cold therapy in Perth? {count} places here list an ice bath or cold plunge, and they fall into three kinds of room. Recovery studios, most of this list, sell the plunge by the session, usually alongside a sauna and often other equipment such as compression boots or red light. Bathhouses and a few day spas include an ice bath in a circuit with a sauna, steam room or hot bath. And a handful of gyms, yoga and Pilates studios keep a plunge beside the training floor.

The biggest difference between them is whether you share. Some sessions are communal, with a group in the same sauna and pools at a set time, often for a flat hour; others are booked as a private room for one or two people, and a few places can be hired outright for a group. Each listing says which where the place publishes it.

Where a session price is published, a sauna-and-plunge block starts at about $25 for thirty minutes and an hour runs about $35 to $45, with cheaper early-morning sessions at some rooms and packs or memberships at most. Each place sets its own prices and they change, so check before you go.

Swimwear is required at communal bathhouses, towels and change rooms vary, and some places set a minimum age. Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: How much does an ice bath cost in Perth?
faq.a: Where it's published, a sauna-and-cold-plunge session starts at about $25 for thirty minutes and runs to about $45 for a private hour, with cheaper early-morning sessions at some rooms and packs or memberships at most. Each place sets its own price, and the listing shows it where the place publishes one.

faq.q: Is an ice bath the same as a cold plunge?
faq.a: Perth places use the two names for the same thing: cold water you sit in for a short time. Some use chilled plunge pools, others ice baths or ice showers, and one beach-based operator uses the ocean itself. This page lists them all together.

faq.q: Is an ice bath the same as cryotherapy?
faq.a: No. An ice bath or cold plunge is cold water you sit in. Cryotherapy means standing in a chamber of very cold, dry air for a few minutes, and only a handful of Perth recovery studios offer it. They have their own page: cryotherapy in Perth.

faq.q: Can I book an ice bath privately?
faq.a: Yes, at several places. Some rooms are booked for one person or a pair, and a few can be hired outright for a group; others run communal sessions at set times. The listing says which where the place publishes it.

faq.q: What should I bring?
faq.a: Usually swimwear, which is required at communal bathhouses. Showers, towels and change rooms are common but not universal, so check the place's own website before your first visit.

faq.q: Where can I do an ice bath and sauna together?
faq.a: Most places on this page pair the plunge with a sauna. The ones set up for alternating the two in one session are also listed under Ice bath & sauna together (contrast therapy).

intro: A sauna and an ice bath in one visit is what the recovery studios call contrast therapy. Sessions alternate heat and cold in one booking: a sauna or hot plunge, then an ice bath or cold plunge, repeated in rounds. {count} places in Perth say on their own websites that they run sessions this way.

The format varies more than the name suggests. Some rooms are booked privately for an hour for one or two people; one suburban studio opens from 5am to 9pm, early enough for before work; a dedicated recovery centre pairs a magnesium hot plunge with cold plunge pools; and a beachside operator runs communal hour-long sessions where, at some sites, the cold water is the ocean.

Where prices are published, a private one-hour session is $45 for one and $80 for two at one studio, and thirty minutes in an infrared sauna starts at $25 at another. Packs and memberships bring the per-visit cost down at most places.
Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: What is contrast therapy?
faq.a: Alternating heat and cold in one session, usually a sauna or hot pool and then an ice bath or cold plunge, repeated a few times. How many rounds, and how long each lasts, is set by each place and often left to you.

faq.q: Where can I do an ice bath and sauna in Perth?
faq.a: The {count} places on this page run both for contrast sessions. Many more have one or the other: see Ice baths & cold plunges and Saunas in Perth.

faq.q: How much does a contrast session cost?
faq.a: Where it's published: a private hour is $45 for one and $80 for two at one Perth studio, and thirty minutes of sauna starts at $25 at another. Most places sell packs and memberships that lower the price per visit.

faq.q: Can I book privately or as a group?
faq.a: Both exist. Some places book the room privately for one or two people, several take group bookings or can be hired outright, and others run communal sessions at set times.

intro: A traditional sauna heats the air in a wood-lined room, and in Perth it turns up in four quite different settings: dedicated sauna houses and studios; communal saunas beside the beach; bathhouses, where it's one stop in a circuit with a steam room and baths; and hotel and day spas, where it usually comes with a treatment or a day visit, often in separate men's and women's areas.

Most of the {count} places here pair the heat with cold water, whether an ice bath, a cold plunge or a magnesium pool, and one sauna house runs its sessions around aufguss, where a facilitator works steam and scent through the room in rounds.

Where prices are published, a sauna-and-plunge session starts at about $25 for thirty minutes and an hour is about $35, and one Subiaco room discounts its 5am to 7am sessions. Communal beachside sessions often run a flat hour.

Bring swimwear for communal and bathhouse sessions, check whether towels are supplied, and note that some places set a minimum age: sixteen at one hotel spa, eighteen at one bathhouse. Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: Where is there a Finnish sauna in Perth?
faq.a: Several places on this page describe their sauna as Finnish, including a sauna house built around aufguss sessions, a communal bathhouse and a dedicated recovery centre. Each listing says what kind of sauna it has.

faq.q: Are there saunas at the beach in Perth?
faq.a: Yes. Beachside operators run communal sauna sessions at several Perth beaches, including Scarborough, City Beach, Cottesloe and South Beach, and at some sites the ocean is the cold plunge.

faq.q: How long is a sauna session?
faq.a: Usually booked as a block. Thirty minutes and an hour are the most common lengths published, and communal beachside sessions often run a flat hour.

faq.q: Can day visitors use a hotel spa's sauna?
faq.a: At some. At least one CBD hotel spa is open to day visitors as well as hotel guests; others are by appointment with a treatment. Check the listing and the spa's own website.

intro: {count} places in Perth list an infrared sauna, and most of them book the cabin privately: you have the room to yourself, or share it with one other person, for a timed session. That is the main practical difference from a traditional sauna, which runs at a much higher air temperature and is more often a shared room.

Most are recovery studios, where the sauna sits beside an ice bath, red light or compression boots and can be booked with them. The rest are day spas and float centres that offer it alongside other treatments, plus a few physio and Pilates studios. One Claremont clinic uses a one-person pod with your head outside instead of a cabin.

Where a single-session price is published, thirty minutes costs $25 to $40 at most places, and $25 at studios in Beldon and Cockburn Central. Forty-five minutes is usually $35 to $50. Bringing a second person into the cabin generally adds $10 to $30 rather than doubling the price. Several studios publish only packs or memberships, and sauna-and-ice-bath sessions are priced separately. Prices were checked on the places' own websites in October 2026, and each place sets its own, so check before you book.

Because most cabins are private, light clothing, swimwear or a towel is the norm. Bring water, and check whether towels are supplied. Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: How much does an infrared sauna cost in Perth?
faq.a: Where a single-session price is published, thirty minutes costs $25 to $40 at most places, and forty-five minutes $35 to $50. The lowest published price is $25 for thirty minutes, at Zen Zone in Beldon and Rhema Wellness Studio in Cockburn Central. Prices checked October 2026 on the places' own websites.

faq.q: How long is an infrared sauna session?
faq.a: Most Perth studios sell thirty- or forty-five-minute sessions, and some offer sixty. A combined sauna-and-ice-bath session usually runs an hour.

faq.q: What do you wear in an infrared sauna?
faq.a: Most infrared cabins in Perth are booked privately, so light clothing, swimwear or a towel is usual. Bring water, and check the place's website for whether towels are supplied.

faq.q: Can two people share an infrared sauna?
faq.a: Yes, at many places. Published two-person prices for thirty minutes include $40 at Zen Zone, $44 at The Neighbourhood Sauna, $45 at Rhema Wellness Studio and $50 at Salt Float Studio.

faq.q: Is an infrared sauna the same as a traditional sauna?
faq.a: No. A traditional sauna heats the air in a wood-lined room and runs much hotter, often as a shared room. An infrared cabin runs at a lower air temperature, is usually private, and sessions tend to be longer. Our infrared vs traditional sauna comparison sets them side by side.

faq.q: Where can I do an infrared sauna and ice bath together?
faq.a: Many recovery studios sell the two as one session. Locked In Recovery in Warwick, for example, publishes sixty minutes of sauna and ice bath for $45. The ice bath and sauna page lists every place that offers both.

intro: Compare what a steam room visit costs, what it includes and who can go, at the places Oria Haven lists. Each card and the table below show the standard adult visit that includes the steam room, as the venue publishes it, with the day it was checked.

Steam rooms in Perth usually come with something larger: a leisure centre's pool and wellness entry, a bathhouse session with saunas and cold pools, a hotel spa's retreat area, or a recovery centre's timed session. A few day spas sell steam on its own. How you get in -- a casual ticket, a treatment, a membership -- differs as much as the price.

A steam room (some places call it a steam sauna) is humid heat at a lower temperature than a sauna's dry heat. It is not the same as a steam shower, or water poured on a sauna's stones; the places here have a steam room. Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: What's the difference between a steam room and a sauna?
faq.a: A steam room fills with humid, wet heat at a lower temperature; a sauna is drier and hotter, though water poured on the stones adds steam. Saunas are listed on Saunas in Perth.

faq.q: How much does a steam room cost in Perth?
faq.a: At a leisure centre the steam room comes with the pools, spa or sauna for one casual entry: Aqualife in East Victoria Park lists $8.20 for adult swim entry with the steam room and spa, Cannington Leisureplex $13 for its adult wellness suite and Beatty Park $18.50 for spa, sauna and steam with pool access. Recovery studios and bathhouses charge more for a timed session with hot and cold pools: Recwell in Wangara $39, Reclab in Wembley $42, Merse Wellness in Osborne Park $59.95 and Ember Bath House $89 for 90 minutes. Revive Skin Emporium sells a 30-minute steam room session for $45. These are the prices each venue published when we checked in September 2026; the table above shows the date for each.

faq.q: What do you wear in a steam room?
faq.a: Swimwear, at the places that say. Ember Bath House requires it, Merse Wellness recommends it, and Crown Spa asks for swimwear or the robes and towels it provides in its shared Aqua Retreat. Rules differ, so check the venue's own page before you go.

faq.q: How old do you have to be to use a steam room?
faq.a: It depends on the venue. Beatty Park and Cannington Leisureplex sell their steam room entry to adults 16 and over, Merse Wellness takes 16 and 17-year-olds with an adult, Crown Spa's minimum is 16 and Ember Bath House is 18 and over. Aqualife says age restrictions apply without stating them.

faq.q: Is there a steam room with a sauna and ice bath in Perth?
faq.a: Yes. Ember Bath House and Merse Wellness sell bathhouse sessions that include saunas, hot pools and an ice bath as well as the steam room, and Reclab in Wembley and Recwell in Wangara include it in their hot-and-cold contrast sessions.

intro: {count} places in Perth list cryotherapy: Perth Cryo in Currambine, Element Health Centres in Claremont, Mindbody Lounge in Victoria Park and Recovery Haus in Innaloo. It is not an ice bath. Instead of sitting in cold water, you stand in a chamber of very cold, dry air for a few minutes. Element Health Centres, for example, runs whole-body sessions of up to three minutes at temperatures down to −87.5°C. Some places also offer localised cryotherapy, which cools one area rather than the whole body.

All four are recovery studios rather than cryotherapy-only clinics, so the chamber sits alongside things like an infrared sauna, compression boots, red light or hyperbaric oxygen. Most sell it in packs or memberships that cover several of them.

Where prices are published, Mindbody Lounge sells session credits that work out at $33 to $40 a session depending on the pack, and Perth Cryo's packages start from $60. Element Health Centres sells weekly memberships and multi-week programmes rather than single sessions. Prices change, so check with the place before you book.
Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: Is cryotherapy the same as an ice bath?
faq.a: No. Cryotherapy is a few minutes in a chamber of very cold, dry air; an ice bath or cold plunge is cold water you sit in. If you're after cold water, see ice baths and cold plunges in Perth.

faq.q: How long is a cryotherapy session?
faq.a: Short. Element Health Centres publishes sessions of up to three minutes. Most places don't publish a length, so ask when you book.

faq.q: How much does cryotherapy cost in Perth?
faq.a: Where it's published, Mindbody Lounge's session credits work out at $33 to $40 a session, and Perth Cryo's packages start from $60. Some places only sell memberships or programmes. Check the place's own site for current prices.

faq.q: Where can I try cryotherapy in Perth?
faq.a: Perth Cryo in Currambine, Element Health Centres in Claremont, Mindbody Lounge in Victoria Park and Recovery Haus in Innaloo all list it. Each listing links to the place's own booking page.

intro: {count} places in Perth list red light therapy. Almost all are recovery studios, float centres or wellness spas that offer it beside a sauna, ice bath or compression boots. It is a light session, not a cold one, so if you came looking for cold therapy, ice baths and cold plunges have their own page.

The equipment varies. Several places use a full-body bed you lie in, such as the TheraLight 360 at Mindbody Lounge in Victoria Park and the full-body bed at Reclab in Wembley. Element Health Centres publishes 20-minute full-body sessions. Others use smaller targeted devices, like the handheld units at My Recovery Club in Harrisdale, and Beyond Rest in East Perth offers red light as a body-contouring service.

Single-session prices are rarely published. Red light is usually sold in packs or memberships that cover several pieces of equipment; Mindbody Lounge's session credits, for example, work out at $33 to $40 a session. Check the place's own site for current prices.

faq.q: How long is a red light session?

faq.q: How much does red light therapy cost in Perth?

intro: {count} places in Perth run a hyperbaric chamber, and they are not all the same machine. A hard-shell chamber is a sealed capsule you lie in while it is pressurised, usually to between 1.3 and 2.0 atmospheres (ATA). Hyper O2 in Kardinya and Studio2 HBOT in Applecross run hard-shell chambers only. Thrive Wellness Centre has both: a one-person soft-shell chamber at about 1.3 ATA and a hard-shell chamber big enough for two. Recovery Haus in Innaloo sells what it calls mild HBOT, up to 1.35 ATA, and Element Health Centres in Claremont has a lie-down chamber and a seated one.

A session is an hour or ninety minutes at most places, and thirty or sixty minutes at Recovery Haus. Oxygen usually comes through a mask or nasal cannula; at Thrive the mask is optional and charged as an extra. Before the first session most clinics take you through a health questionnaire or a short consult.

A casual hour costs $100 to $120 at four of the five, and $75 in Recovery Haus's milder chamber. Some first sessions are cheaper — Studio2 HBOT charges $60 for a first hour. Packs bring the price down a long way: Thrive's 20-session soft-shell pack works out at $30 a session and its hard-shell pack at $55, against $85 at Studio2 HBOT and $99 for ten at Hyper O2. Prices change, so check the clinic's own site before you book.

These are private wellness clinics, not hospital units. Several of their websites describe what a chamber is meant to do for particular conditions; Oria Haven doesn't repeat those claims, and none of the five publishes a Medicare rebate. Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: How much does hyperbaric oxygen therapy cost in Perth?
faq.a: A single 60-minute session is $100 to $120 at most Perth clinics, and $75 in Recovery Haus's mild chamber. Studio2 HBOT charges $60 for a first hour. In packs it falls to $30 a session in Thrive's soft-shell chamber, $55 in its hard-shell one, $85 at Studio2 HBOT and $99 at Hyper O2. Prices were checked on each clinic's own site in October 2026.

faq.q: What is the difference between a hard-shell and a soft-shell chamber?
faq.a: Pressure, mainly. The hard-shell chambers in Perth run at 1.3 to 2.0 ATA. Thrive's soft-shell chamber runs at about 1.3 ATA, and Recovery Haus's mild chamber at up to 1.35. Soft-shell and mild sessions are the cheaper ones.

faq.q: Do I need a referral?
faq.a: None of the five clinics says you need a GP referral. Most screen you first with a health questionnaire or a consult, and Thrive says it may refer you to your GP after reviewing yours.

faq.q: How long is a session?
faq.a: Usually 60 or 90 minutes. Recovery Haus sells 30 and 60-minute sessions.

faq.q: Can two people go in together?
faq.a: At Thrive Wellness Centre, yes: its hard-shell chamber takes two, at $150 for an hour. Studio2 HBOT has two one-person chambers you can book side by side, and Hyper O2 lets a friend book at the same time.

faq.q: Is it covered by Medicare?
faq.a: None of the five clinics on this page publishes a Medicare rebate. If you have private health cover, ask your fund what it pays for, and before you book rather than after.

faq.q: Where can I try a hyperbaric chamber in Perth?
faq.a: Element Health Centres in Claremont, Hyper O2 in Kardinya, Recovery Haus in Innaloo, Studio2 HBOT in Applecross and Thrive Wellness Centre all list one. Each listing links to the clinic's own booking page.

intro: {count} day spas in Perth are listed here, from a single treatment room in a suburban strip to hotel spas with their own pools. What makes a place a day spa rather than a massage clinic is the time: treatments are booked back to back — a massage, a facial, a body treatment — with a robe and a quiet room in between, and most sell that as a package of two hours or more.

Hotel spas sit at the top. Crown Spa Perth at Crown Towers has an Aqua Retreat with a vitality pool, sauna and steam room, and The Ritz-Carlton Spa at Elizabeth Quay has vitality pools and a sauna. Solace Day Spa in Scarborough added a bathhouse — magnesium bath, ice bath and sauna — to its treatment rooms. In the hills and the Swan Valley, Hidden Valley Eco Lodges, Amaroo Retreat & Spa and Swan Valley Retreat pair the spa with somewhere to stay, so a day can turn into a night.

A 60-minute relaxation massage at a suburban day spa costs $100 to $195, and $169 is the middle of the 15 that publish one. The hotel spas start higher: Crown from $250 an hour, and the Ritz-Carlton's shortest massage is 75 minutes for $275. Packages of two hours or more start at $160, and most sit between $260 and $450.

Read what a package holds, not just how long it is. One two-hour package on this page includes thirty minutes of massage; the rest is sauna and lounge time. Some places add a weekend surcharge — endota spa Joondalup adds 5% on Saturdays and 10% on Sundays — and package names change with the season, so the one you saw last month may be gone. Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: How much does a day spa cost in Perth?
faq.a: A 60-minute relaxation massage is $100 to $195 at most suburban day spas, with $169 the middle price. Packages of two hours or more start at $160 and mostly run $260 to $450. The hotel spas cost more: Crown Spa Perth from $250 an hour, The Ritz-Carlton Spa $275 for 75 minutes. Prices were checked on each spa's own site in October 2026.

faq.q: What's the difference between a day spa and a massage clinic?
faq.a: Time and setting. A massage clinic books one treatment and you leave; a day spa books several in a row, with robes, a relaxation room and often a sauna or pool between them. Massage clinics are usually cheaper per hour, and some do remedial massage you can claim on a health fund.

faq.q: Which Perth day spas have a pool or sauna?
faq.a: Crown Spa Perth (vitality pool, sauna, steam room) and The Ritz-Carlton Spa (vitality pools, sauna) at the hotel end; Solace Day Spa in Scarborough (magnesium bath, ice bath, sauna); Swan Valley Retreat (sauna and ice bath); and Urban Retreat Day Spa in Rockingham and Le Beau Clinic & Spa in Kardinya, which both have a sauna.

faq.q: Can we go as a couple?

faq.q: Are day spas open on Sundays?

faq.q: Is the price for two people?

intro: {count} places in Perth list Thai massage. Jade Clinic in the city, Perth Thai Massage in Bedford, Tara Massage Therapy and Royal Silk Remedial Thai Massage in Rockingham are Thai-led clinics with long massage menus. Aurora Therapeutic Massage in Joondalup offers Thai yoga massage, with one of its therapists only.

Royal Silk takes $10 off massages of an hour or more booked between 8am and 2pm and adds 10% on public holidays, and Tara takes a $60 deposit with every booking. All five open on Sundays.

faq.q: How much is a Thai massage in Perth?

faq.q: What happens in a Thai massage?
faq.a: You stay clothed and there's no oil. The therapist uses pressure along the body and moves you through assisted stretches. Thai aromatherapy massage is different: it uses oil and long strokes, closer to a relaxation massage.

faq.q: Is Thai yoga massage the same thing?
faq.a: It's a name some places use for the same style, stressing the stretching. Aurora Therapeutic Massage in Joondalup lists it, with one therapist.

faq.q: Can I get a Thai massage on a Sunday?

intro: {count} dietitians and dietitian practices in Perth are listed here. A dietitian is not the same as a nutritionist: an Accredited Practising Dietitian holds a university degree in dietetics and is credentialed by Dietitians Australia, and that credential is what lets them see you under a Medicare care plan.

Most specialise. Dietetic Gut Clinic works only on gut problems with FODMAP-trained dietitians; Nutrition Nation in Claremont focuses on fertility, PCOS and endometriosis; Intuitry takes a non-diet approach to eating-disorder recovery; Perth Performance Nutrition and Nutrition Works lean towards sport; and Katie Lenhoff Nutrition works mainly in kidney and heart nutrition. Twelve of the fourteen offer telehealth, so what a practice specialises in matters more than where it is.

A first consultation costs $160 to $320, and $210 is the middle of the 11 practices that publish one. Follow-ups are shorter and cheaper, $95 to $220 and typically about $115. Under a GP care plan, Medicare pays a rebate towards a limited number of allied health visits a year; nine practices here say they take those referrals, several take eating-disorder plan referrals too, and most list private health fund rebates.
Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: How much does a dietitian cost in Perth?
faq.a: A first consultation is $160 to $320, with $210 the middle price across the 11 practices that publish one. Follow-ups typically cost about $115. Nutrition Works in Lathlain is the cheapest first visit at $160. Prices were checked on each practice's own site or booking page in October 2026.

faq.q: What's the difference between a dietitian and a nutritionist?
faq.a: An Accredited Practising Dietitian has a university degree in dietetics and is credentialed by Dietitians Australia. That credential is what Medicare and most health funds recognise. Nutritionist is a broader title with no single required qualification, so check what any practitioner holds before you book.

faq.q: Can I see a dietitian on Medicare?
faq.a: With a care plan from your GP, Medicare pays a rebate towards a limited number of allied health visits a year, which can include a dietitian. Nine practices on this page say they take those referrals. You usually still pay a gap.

faq.q: Can I see a dietitian online?

faq.q: Which Perth dietitians work with PCOS, IBS or low FODMAP?

intro: {count} places in Perth offer reiki. In a session you lie clothed on a table in a quiet room while the practitioner rests their hands lightly on or just above you, usually for about an hour. intro: {count} practitioners in Perth prescribe herbal medicine, from three traditions: naturopaths, who mostly use Western herbs alongside diet advice; Chinese medicine practitioners, usually alongside acupuncture; and Ayurvedic practitioners. The tradition shapes the consultation as much as the herbs, so it's worth choosing that first.

A first consultation costs $50 to $245, and $115 is the middle of the 15 Perth practices that publish one. The traditions sit at different prices: Chinese medicine clinics charge least for the consult, about $70 for a first visit; naturopaths about $140; Ayurvedic practitioners $99 to $245. Follow-ups cost $30 to $125.

The herbs are usually extra. Six clinics say so outright: a week's Chinese herbal formula is about $25 to $60 at the two TCM clinics that publish it, and Cottesloe Naturopathic Clinic quotes about $65 to $120 for remedies. Ask what a typical prescription costs before you book. If you take prescription medicine, tell both the practitioner and your GP before you start.

faq.q: Are the herbs included in the consultation fee?

intro: {count} studios, clubs and arts centres in Perth teach pottery to adults, and the first choice is wheel or hand-building. On the wheel you throw a pot on a spinning wheel: harder than it looks, and the part most people come to try. Hand-building means pinching, coiling and slab work at a table, slower and more forgiving. Most places here teach both; Perth Pottery Co, Winterwares and Happy Hub Collective lead with hand-building.

The easiest start is a one-off taster, and $120 is the middle of the 15 studios that publish one. The cheapest are Terraform Studio’s Thursday wheel session in Mandurah ($75, firing $25 a piece extra), three hours on the wheel at ClayMake in Maylands ($80) and the wheel intros at Studio P in Mount Hawthorn and the South of the River Potters’ Club in Alfred Cove ($95). At the top, House of Hobby’s wheel-and-wine night in West Perth is $165 and Not Yet Perfect’s two hours on the wheel in Applecross $179. What you make is fired and ready to collect two to six weeks later.

To learn properly, take a course of four to eight weekly classes; $395 is the middle price across 17 studios. Community studios and clubs are the cheapest by the hour, at $14 to $20 an hour of tuition: Canning Arts Group ($345 for eight three-hour classes, clay and firing extra), Fremantle Arts Centre ($394, clay included), the South of the River Potters’ Club ($400), Perth Studio Potters in Cottesloe ($360), Midland Junction Arts Centre ($455) and Rockingham Ceramics Studio ($395). Private studios work out at $25 to $58 an hour.

Fremantle has the most choice: Hound Ceramics, Winterwares, Happy Hub Collective and the arts centre in Fremantle itself, and Porch Ceramics in North Fremantle. North of the river, look at ClayMake, Studio P, Perth Pottery Co in Inglewood, House of Hobby in West Perth, Earth & KLĀ in Wembley and Potteroo in Mount Claremont; south, at MUK Studio in O’Connor, Not Yet Perfect, From Dust Studio in Willetton and the South of the River Potters’ Club. Further out, Terraform Studio is on the Mandurah foreshore and Rockingham Ceramics Studio sits behind the Rockingham Arts Centre.

Book well ahead. On 13 October, Studio P’s intro workshops were sold out until the end of November, Rockingham Ceramics Studio’s classes were all full, and most of Fremantle Arts Centre’s ceramics classes, MUK Studio’s six-week course and the South of the River Potters’ Club’s eight-week course had sold out. Several studios are 18+ (House of Hobby, Midland Junction Arts Centre, Perth Studio Potters, Fremantle Arts Centre) and Hound Ceramics is 16+.

faq.q: How much is a pottery class in Perth?
faq.a: A one-off taster is $75 to $179, and $120 is the middle of the 15 studios that publish one; the cheapest in the metro area is $80 for three hours on the wheel at ClayMake in Maylands. Beginner courses of four to eight weeks cost $290 to $999, typically about $395, and community clubs are the cheapest by the hour. Prices were checked on each studio’s own site in October 2026.

faq.q: Should I start on the wheel or with hand-building?
faq.a: The wheel is what most beginners want to try, and most tasters are wheel sessions. Hand-building (pinching, coiling, slabs) is slower and more forgiving: Perth Pottery Co, Winterwares and Happy Hub Collective lead with it. Most studios teach both.

faq.q: Are there pottery classes for couples in Perth?
faq.a: Yes. From Dust Studio in Willetton has a Me + Friend wheel session for $254, Terraform Studio in Mandurah a Wine & Wheels night for $329 for two, and Not Yet Perfect in Applecross a couple ticket for $375. House of Hobby runs a pottery date night at $155 a person, held off-site in Burswood. Elsewhere, book two places in a taster.

faq.q: Where can I paint pottery in Perth?
faq.a: Happy Hub Collective in Fremantle is the only studio on this page with paint-your-own pottery: $98 a guest for a session, or $89 for a plate ($59 for children). The other studios teach making rather than painting finished pieces.

faq.q: Are there pottery classes in Fremantle?
faq.a: More than anywhere else in Perth: Hound Ceramics, Winterwares, Happy Hub Collective and Fremantle Arts Centre in Fremantle, and Porch Ceramics in North Fremantle. MUK Studio in O’Connor and the South of the River Potters’ Club in Alfred Cove are close by.

faq.q: Are there pottery classes in Mandurah or Rockingham?
faq.a: Terraform Studio on the Mandurah foreshore runs a $75 Thursday wheel session and three- and six-week courses, and Rockingham Ceramics Studio, a volunteer-run community studio behind the Rockingham Arts Centre, runs adult term courses ($395 hand-building, $520 wheel). Rockingham’s classes were full in mid-October.

faq.q: How long until I get my pottery back?
faq.a: Two to six weeks, because pieces are dried, fired and glazed after the class. Studio P and Winterwares say about three weeks, ClayMake about two (bisque firing only), and Hound Ceramics and Perth Pottery Co about six. At Terraform and Earth & KLĀ, firing is charged on top of the session.

faq.q: Can I use a pottery studio on my own?
faq.a: Yes, with a membership or a drop-in session once you can throw. Terraform’s membership starts at $29 a week and Studio P’s is $39 a week (three-month minimum); ClayMake’s is $105 a month and Hound Ceramics’ $220. Not Yet Perfect and Happy Hub Collective sell $45 drop-in sessions.

intro: {count} salons, spas and beauty clinics in Perth list waxing. Most do the full menu (Brazilian and bikini, legs, arms, underarms, brows and face), and a handful are built around it, Brazilian Butterfly on Fremantle’s High Street most of all. Several use hot or hard wax for the Brazilian and bikini line and strip wax for legs: Bali Spirit Day Spa and Bare Skin and Beauty in Ellenbrook and Serendipity Medi Spa in Canning Vale all say so.

A full Brazilian costs $55 to $80 at the salons that publish a price, and $75 is the most common. The cheapest are Manusa Organic Spa & Beauty in East Fremantle ($55) and, north of the river, Oxford Beauty Clinic in Leederville and Bali Spirit in Ellenbrook ($60 each). A standard bikini wax runs $25 to $49, a brow wax $20 to $37, and a full leg about $68. A first Brazilian costs more at some salons: Serendipity charges $79 for a first visit.

Men’s waxing is on most menus but priced separately: a back wax is $45 at Oxford Beauty Clinic to $67 at Brazilian Butterfly, and a chest $40 to $65. Brazilian Butterfly is the only salon here publishing a men’s Brazilian, at $140.

The salons’ own advice on getting ready is consistent: let hair grow to about the length of a grain of rice (Brazilian Butterfly says 5mm to 1cm), exfoliate gently a day or two before, and wear loose cotton clothing to the appointment. Late nights are mostly on Wednesday and Thursday; for a Sunday wax, Bali Spirit opens 10 to 4 and endota spa Joondalup 11 to 5, with a 10% Sunday surcharge at endota.

faq.q: How much is a Brazilian wax in Perth?
faq.a: A full Brazilian costs $55 to $80 at the salons that publish a price, and $75 is the most common. Manusa Organic Spa & Beauty in East Fremantle charges $55; Oxford Beauty Clinic in Leederville and Bali Spirit in Ellenbrook $60. Prices were checked on each salon’s own site or booking page in October 2026.

faq.q: What is a Brazilian wax?
faq.a: Perth salons use it for the full intimate wax, front to back, with nothing left: Brazilian Butterfly calls it “Take it All Off” and Bali Spirit “everything gone”. A bikini wax covers less, and is priced lower. Names vary, so check the description on the salon’s menu.

faq.q: How long does hair need to be for a Brazilian wax?
faq.a: About the length of a grain of rice. Brazilian Butterfly asks for 5mm to 1cm and Serendipity Medi Spa about a quarter of an inch.

faq.q: How do I prepare for a wax?
faq.a: The salons publishing advice say to exfoliate gently a day or two before (Brazilian Butterfly, Serendipity Medi Spa, endota spa), skip moisturiser on the day, and wear loose cotton clothing to the appointment.

faq.q: Where can men get waxed in Perth?
faq.a: Most salons on this page wax men. Back waxes run $45 (Oxford Beauty Clinic) to $67 (Brazilian Butterfly), chest waxes $40 to $65; Bare Skin and Beauty, Essence of Lily, Serendipity Medi Spa and endota spa Joondalup all publish men’s prices. Brazilian Butterfly is the only one publishing a men’s Brazilian, at $140.

faq.q: Can I get waxed on a Sunday in Perth?
faq.a: At a few places. Bali Spirit Day Spa in Ellenbrook opens 10 to 4 and endota spa Joondalup 11 to 5 (with a 10% Sunday surcharge). Most salons are closed on Sundays but open late on Wednesday or Thursday.

faq.q: Where can I get waxed in Fremantle?
faq.a: Brazilian Butterfly on High Street, plus A Touch of Sass, Manusa Organic Spa & Beauty and Pamper Face and Body nearby in East and South Fremantle.

bathhouse.title: Bathhouses in Perth: Compare {count} Places & Prices
bathhouse.description: Compare {count} bathhouses in Perth, from Ember in Osborne Park to Scarborough and Fremantle: saunas, hot and ice baths, prices and who can go.
intro: A bathhouse in Perth is a circuit of heat and water in one booking: a sauna, a hot mineral or magnesium bath, an ice bath and, at some, a steam room. {count} places here sell one, and the biggest difference between them is how many people you share it with.

Ember Bath House in Osborne Park is the large communal one: 90 minutes with a Finnish sauna, steam room, hot mineral bath and ice bath for $89, with a towel, robe and tea. It is all-gender, swimwear is required and it's 18 and over. Merse Wellness, also in Osborne Park, sells a 60-minute bathhouse session for $59.95, with magnesium pools, infrared and hot rock saunas, a steam room and an ice bath; 16 and 17-year-olds can go with an adult.

Two are smaller. Solace Day Spa on the Scarborough Esplanade runs its bathhouse by the hour for up to four guests at a time, $69 a session, or $259 to have it to yourselves for up to six. The Neighbourhood Sauna on South Terrace, Fremantle, books its Bath House Experience as a private room with an infrared sauna, hot magnesium bath and ice bath, $75 for one or $140 for two.

Prices are as each venue published them when we checked in September and October 2026. Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: How much is a bathhouse in Perth?
faq.a: A session costs $59.95 for an hour at Merse Wellness, $69 at Solace Day Spa, $75 at The Neighbourhood Sauna and $89 for 90 minutes at Ember Bath House, as each published it when we checked in October 2026. All four sell multi-visit packs, and Ember, Merse and The Neighbourhood Sauna also sell memberships.

faq.q: What's included at Ember Bath House?
faq.a: Ninety minutes with a Finnish sauna, steam room, hot mineral bath and ice bath, with a towel, robe and tea, for $89. It is all-gender, swimwear is required and it's 18 and over. Ember also runs a silent session at the same price, sessions for two at $178, and packages that add a massage or a hammam ritual.

faq.q: Is there a bathhouse in Osborne Park?
faq.a: Two. Ember Bath House on Donovan Street is the larger communal bathhouse, and Merse Wellness sells a 60-minute bathhouse session with magnesium pools, saunas, a steam room and an ice bath.

faq.q: Can I book a private bathhouse in Perth?
faq.a: Yes. The Neighbourhood Sauna's Bath House Experience in Fremantle is a private room for one or two people, and Solace Day Spa in Scarborough sells a private bathhouse session for up to six for $259. Solace's standard sessions take at most four guests.

faq.q: What do you wear to a bathhouse?
faq.a: Swimwear at Ember Bath House, where it's required, and at Merse Wellness, which recommends it and hires towels for $4.95. In The Neighbourhood Sauna's private rooms, comfortable clothing or a swimsuit is fine. Check each venue's own page before you go.

faq.q: How old do you have to be to go to a bathhouse?
faq.a: Ember Bath House is 18 and over. Merse Wellness takes 16 and 17-year-olds with an adult, and The Neighbourhood Sauna's minimum age is 12. Solace doesn't state one on its bathhouse page.

cat:yoga.description: Compare {count} yoga studios in Perth: hot, vinyasa, yin, pregnancy and beginners' classes, with intro passes from $39 checked on each studio's site.
intro: {count} yoga studios and teachers in Perth are listed here, from timetabled studios to weekly classes in community halls. Fremantle and the southern suburbs have the most, then central Perth, with a handful each in the northern and western suburbs and the hills.

Yin and vinyasa are the most common styles. For heat, four studios run hot classes: The Yoga Garage in Scarborough, which lists Bikram alongside hot vinyasa and yin, Hot For Yoga in Jandakot, Flow Hot Yoga & Pilates in Wangara and The Studio Perth in East Victoria Park. AirSpace in Leederville teaches aerial yoga, with orientation sessions before your first aerial class.

For pregnancy yoga, Small Blessings Yoga in Beaconsfield, Bloom Yoga Studio in Kingsley, Yoga Corner in Duncraig, Tamara Yoga in Claremont, The Yoga Space in West Perth and Bodyscape in Nedlands list prenatal classes. Tamara Yoga, Bloom Yoga Studio and Kookaburra Yoga in Bedfordale run yoga teacher training.

The easiest way to start is an intro pass for new students: The Yoga Garage and Yogahub in Mount Hawthorn advertise 14 days for $39, Hot For Yoga 25 days for $49, Horizon Yoga in Cottesloe 21 days and Yoga Corner 30 days for $59 each, and Bodyscape 14 days for $69, as each studio published them when checked in October 2026. Most can be bought once per person.

faq.q: How much is a yoga class in Perth?
faq.a: Most studios sell intro passes, class packs and memberships rather than one class price. The intro passes listed here cost $39 to $69 for 14 to 30 days of classes, as each studio published them in October 2026; after that, check each studio's own timetable and price list.

faq.q: Where can I do hot yoga in Perth?
faq.a: Four studios here run hot classes: The Yoga Garage in Scarborough, Hot For Yoga in Jandakot, Flow Hot Yoga & Pilates in Wangara and The Studio Perth in East Victoria Park.

faq.q: Is there Bikram yoga in Perth?
faq.a: The Yoga Garage in Scarborough lists Bikram classes alongside hot vinyasa, yin and hot core Pilates, and its intro pass covers all of them.

faq.q: Where can I try aerial yoga in Perth?
faq.a: AirSpace in Leederville teaches aerial yoga. New students can take a 14-day trial of unlimited group classes, which includes orientation sessions before the first aerial class.

faq.q: Where can I do pregnancy yoga in Perth?
faq.a: Small Blessings Yoga in Beaconsfield, Bloom Yoga Studio in Kingsley, Yoga Corner in Duncraig, Tamara Yoga in Claremont, The Yoga Space in West Perth and Bodyscape in Nedlands list prenatal classes. If you're unsure whether yoga suits you in pregnancy, ask your midwife or GP first.

faq.q: Where can I do yoga teacher training in Perth?
faq.a: Tamara Yoga in Claremont, Bloom Yoga Studio in Kingsley and Kookaburra Yoga in Bedfordale run teacher training. Course length, accreditation and dates are on each studio's own site.

yoga@fremantle.title: Yoga in Fremantle: Studios, Classes & Prices
yoga@fremantle.description: Yoga in Fremantle, East and North Fremantle: YOGALAB on High Street, Yogaveda, Fremantle Yoga Centre and Loop Yoga, with styles, courses and prices.
intro: In Fremantle itself, YOGALAB on High Street calls its 200-square-metre room the largest yoga studio in Western Australia, and Yogaveda Wellness Centre has run daily classes, from gentle to dynamic, alongside an Ayurvedic clinic since 2008. Lakshmi Ayurveda, in a Fremantle cottage, teaches yoga classes beside its Ayurvedic treatments, and Oversoul Studio on Wood Street runs a weekly stretch class and monthly yoga and sound bath events.

Two of the area's best-known studios sit just over the suburb line. Fremantle Yoga Centre on Petra Street, East Fremantle, one of Perth's longest-standing studios, teaches vinyasa, hatha, beginners, therapy yoga, restorative yin and mum-and-bubs classes. Loop Yoga in North Fremantle runs from power yoga and sculpt Pilates to yin, restorative and yoga nidra with live crystal bowls; drop-ins are $32 and memberships start at $39 a week.

New to yoga: Yogaveda runs six-week beginner courses from $126 prepaid, and Fremantle Yoga Centre has beginners' classes on its timetable. For pregnancy yoga, Small Blessings Yoga in nearby Beaconsfield teaches pregnancy and postnatal yoga in ten-week courses that follow the school terms.

faq.q: Where can I do yoga in Fremantle?
faq.a: In Fremantle: YOGALAB on High Street, Yogaveda Wellness Centre, Lakshmi Ayurveda and Oversoul Studio on Wood Street. Close by: Fremantle Yoga Centre in East Fremantle and Loop Yoga in North Fremantle.

faq.q: Is there a beginners' yoga course in Fremantle?
faq.a: Yogaveda Wellness Centre runs six-week beginner courses from $126 prepaid, and Fremantle Yoga Centre in East Fremantle has beginners' classes on its timetable.

faq.q: How much is a yoga class in Fremantle?
faq.a: Loop Yoga in North Fremantle lists drop-in classes at $32 and memberships from $39 a week, and Yogaveda's six-week beginner course is $126 prepaid. Other studios publish their prices on their own timetables.

faq.q: Is there pregnancy yoga near Fremantle?
faq.a: Small Blessings Yoga in Beaconsfield teaches pregnancy and postnatal yoga, and Fremantle Yoga Centre in East Fremantle runs mum-and-bubs classes.

faq.q: Where can I do yoga nidra in Fremantle?
faq.a: Yogaveda Wellness Centre runs Friday-evening yoga nidra and deep-restore sessions, and Loop Yoga in North Fremantle holds yoga nidra inside a live crystal-bowl sound session.

yoga@west-perth.title: Yoga in West Perth: The Yoga Space & Studios Nearby
yoga@west-perth.description: Yoga in West Perth: The Yoga Space on Colin Street, plus studios a suburb away in the CBD, West Leederville and Shenton Park, with styles and prices.
intro: West Perth's own yoga studio is The Yoga Space at 6/79 Colin Street, teaching Ashtanga, vinyasa, yin and pregnancy yoga, in person and online, since 2005. Newcomers start with a three-week unlimited introduction, which lets you try each style across the timetable before choosing one.

A suburb away there is more choice. In the CBD, Energy Cntr Yoga on Stirling Street runs vinyasa, hatha, slow flow, yin and power flow in a room for 35, with casual classes at $28. In West Leederville, Vitality House's public studio on Southport Street runs warmed vinyasa, slow flow and power yoga and yin, at $27 a class or $59 for 14 days unlimited. Yoga West, upstairs on Onslow Road in Shenton Park, teaches Iyengar from Foundations upwards, at $30 a class or $85 for a newcomer's first month.
For something different, AirSpace on Newcastle Street, Leederville, is the home of AirYoga, its aerial hammock class, with drop-ins at $39.

faq.q: Where can I do yoga in West Perth?
faq.a: The Yoga Space at 6/79 Colin Street is West Perth's yoga studio, teaching Ashtanga, vinyasa, yin and pregnancy yoga in person and online. Nearby are Energy Cntr Yoga in the CBD, Vitality House in West Leederville and Yoga West in Shenton Park.

faq.q: Is there a beginners' option for yoga near West Perth?
faq.a: The Yoga Space runs a three-week unlimited introduction for newcomers. Yoga West in Shenton Park has Foundations classes you can join at any time, and newcomers can take a month of unlimited classes for $85.

faq.q: How much is a yoga class near West Perth?
faq.a: Published casual prices nearby run from $27 a class at Vitality House in West Leederville to $28 at Energy Cntr Yoga in the CBD and $30 at Yoga West in Shenton Park. Intro offers include 14 days unlimited for $59 at Vitality House. Prices checked October 2026.

faq.q: Is there hot or heated yoga near West Perth?
faq.a: Vitality House in West Leederville runs warmed vinyasa, slow flow and power yoga. For fully heated rooms and Bikram, see the hot yoga page; the nearest are further out.

faq.q: Can I do yoga online with a West Perth studio?
faq.a: Yes. The Yoga Space on Colin Street teaches online as well as in person, so you can keep up when you can't get to the studio.
